finding.claim: A urlencoded Content-Type with parameters (e.g. charset) is not matched by the exact-equality check, so the URLENCODED body processor is never selected and ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY stay empty; body rules are bypassed under default config.
finding.source: Request header Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8 (attacker-controlled), read in AddRequestHeader at transaction.go:376-390.
finding.sink: ARGS_POST / REQUEST_BODY population, only written by urlencoded.go:27-31 and never reached.

trace.note: Content-Type value lowercased
Exact equality with 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' fails for the parameterized value, so reqbodyProcessor is not set to URLENCODED
ProcessRequestBody reads rbp, which is empty
rbp == '' branch evaluates rules without parsing the body; no REQBODY_ERROR is set
ForceRequestBodyVariable defaults to false, so the forced-URLENCODED fallback at transaction.go:1104-1114 does not run

finding.guards_checked: Multipart uses a prefix match (transaction.go:388), so it is not affected. ForceRequestBodyVariable defaults to false (waf.go:210) and can only be enabled by a rule via ctl:forceRequestBodyVariable (ctl.go:203). transaction.go:499 strips parameters only for line-ending logic in ParseRequestReader and does not affect processor selection. Not verified: whether CRS sets forceRequestBodyVariable (CRS not in repo).

finding.claim: Query-string arguments beyond ArgumentLimit (default 1000) are silently dropped with only a debug log, so a payload placed among many padding args may never reach ARGS_GET; the kept subset is randomized by Go map iteration.
finding.source: Query string of the request-target (attacker-controlled), passed to ExtractGetArguments at transaction.go:853.
finding.sink: ARGS_GET population used by rule inspection (AddGetRequestArgument at transaction.go:771-776).

trace.note: ProcessURI calls ExtractGetArguments(parsedURL.RawQuery)
ParseQuery builds a Go map (url.go:36), so iteration order is random
ExtractGetArguments ranges over the map and calls AddGetRequestArgument
checkArgumentLimit returns true once argsGet.Len() >= ArgumentLimit
Argument is skipped with only a debug warning; no interruption or error flag is set
Default ArgumentLimit is 1000

finding.guards_checked: Body processors bypass the cap (urlencoded.go:29, json.go:35, multipart.go:109 call Set directly), so the cap affects only the query string. Payload survival is roughly 1000/N for N distinct query keys. Exploitation requires the server to accept a long request-target.

finding.claim: When url.ParseRequestURI fails (e.g. invalid percent-escape in the path), the query is never extracted, so ARGS_GET and QUERY_STRING stay empty while REQUEST_FILENAME contains the raw query.
finding.source: Request-target with an invalid percent-escape in the path, e.g. /%zz?x=<payload> (attacker-controlled).
finding.sink: ARGS_GET and QUERY_STRING population used by rule inspection.

trace.note: Fragment is cut at '#'
url.ParseRequestURI returns an error for the invalid escape in the path (Go url behavior, assumed not executed)
path = uri, so the raw query is included in the path
ExtractGetArguments is skipped on the error branch
QUERY_STRING is set to empty

finding.guards_checked: Only urlencodedError is set (transaction.go:837), which helps only if a rule checks it. The fallback extraction at transaction.go:840-851 is commented out.

finding.claim: defer temp.Close() inside the per-part loop keeps one file descriptor open per file part until ProcessRequest returns, so a multipart body with many file parts can exhaust the host process's file descriptors.
finding.source: Multipart body containing many file parts, attacker-controlled, up to the 128 MiB default request body limit (waf.go:331).
finding.sink: Host process file descriptor table (os.CreateTemp at multipart.go:64).

trace.note: Loop over NextPart
os.CreateTemp per file part
defer temp.Close() runs only when ProcessRequest returns
CreateTemp failure returns an error, but descriptors are already held

finding.guards_checked: Request body limit only. No file-count or part-count limit exists in the processor. ArgumentLimit does not apply to multipart parts.

finding.claim: The request-target is truncated at '#' before path extraction, so the WAF path view can differ from backends that treat '#' literally and normalize dot segments (e.g. /public#/../admin).
finding.source: Request-target containing '#' followed by dot segments (attacker-controlled).

trace.note: Everything after '#' is removed
WAF path view is /public
Backend, not this library, would resolve /public#/../admin to /admin

finding.guards_checked: None in the library. Exploitability depends on backend acceptance of '#' in the request-target.

finding.claim: Whole request bodies are copied into additional heap buffers by body processors, so each concurrent request can use memory proportional to the body limit, amplified by copies.
finding.source: Request body up to 128 MiB default, attacker-controlled.

trace.note: io.Copy into strings.Builder copies the full body
Full JSON body copied into a strings.Builder
io.ReadAll for non-file fields, unbounded per field

finding.guards_checked: Request body limit (waf.go:331). RequestBodyInMemoryLimit governs only body_buffer.go, not these copies.

finding.claim: JSON values are flattened into a single map where duplicate or dot-colliding keys overwrite earlier values, so the inspected value may differ from a backend that keeps another value.
finding.source: JSON body with duplicate keys or keys colliding after dot-joining (attacker-controlled).

trace.note: Keys are joined with '.', so distinct structures can collide
res map write is last-write-wins
SetIndex copies the surviving value into ARGS_POST

finding.guards_checked: Recursion limit at json.go:106-110 bounds depth only. Exploitability requires backend semantics that differ.

finding.claim: Multipart parse errors stop processing of remaining parts, and the transaction continues rule evaluation on partial variables, so parts after a malformed boundary are not inspected.
finding.source: Malformed multipart boundary or unparseable Content-Type (attacker-controlled).
finding.sink: ARGS_POST and file variables for parts after the malformation.

NextPart error sets MultipartStrictError and returns
Processor error is logged and rules are still evaluated on partial variables

finding.guards_checked: The library does not block. Blocking depends on rules that check REQBODY_ERROR.

finding.source: Read or write error during io.Copy into the temp file (e.g. disk full).
